concepts.name: Customer needs and expectations
concepts.summary: Explain that customers contact you with a goal and expectations such as speed, accuracy, courtesy and a clear outcome.

concepts.name: Courteous greeting and tone
concepts.summary: Recall how to open and close contacts politely, using a warm, respectful tone and the customer's name.

concepts.name: Active listening
concepts.summary: Describe how to give full attention, avoid interrupting and confirm what the customer said by paraphrasing.

concepts.name: Channel characteristics
concepts.summary: Describe how phone, email and chat differ in speed, tone cues and written record.

concepts.name: Clear simple language
concepts.summary: Explain why short, jargon-free wording makes answers easier for customers to understand and act on.

concepts.name: Knowing your limits
concepts.summary: Recall that you should not guess or promise beyond your authority and should know who to ask or hand over to.

misconceptions.text: Good customer service just means being friendly and smiling.
Listening means waiting for the customer to stop talking so you can give the answer.
Using technical terms makes you sound professional and reassures the customer.

concepts.name: Clarifying questions
concepts.summary: Use open and closed questions to uncover the real issue and gather the details needed to help.

concepts.name: Empathy statements
concepts.summary: Apply short, sincere statements that acknowledge the customer's feelings and situation before moving to solutions.

concepts.name: Structured call or chat flow
concepts.summary: Run a contact through opening, diagnosis, resolution and closing, including checking the customer is satisfied.

concepts.name: Setting realistic expectations
concepts.summary: Give honest timeframes and next steps and avoid promises you cannot be sure of keeping.

concepts.name: Writing clear customer emails
concepts.summary: Write replies that answer the question first, are well organised and use an appropriate, courteous tone.

concepts.name: Accurate case notes
concepts.summary: Record each contact factually and completely so a colleague can continue without asking the customer to repeat themselves.

concepts.name: Handling a basic complaint
concepts.summary: Handle a straightforward complaint by listening, apologising, fixing it or offering options, and confirming the outcome.

misconceptions.text: Apologising means admitting the company is at fault and should be avoided.
Promising a fast fix, even if unsure, keeps the customer happy.
Case notes are only for managers, so brief or vague notes are fine.

concepts.name: De-escalating angry customers
concepts.summary: Use calm tone, acknowledgement and focus on solutions to reduce a customer's anger without taking it personally.

concepts.name: Root-cause diagnosis
concepts.summary: Analyse symptoms and customer information to separate the real cause from the stated complaint.

concepts.name: Service recovery
concepts.summary: Analyse a service failure and choose an apology, fix and fair compensation that restores trust.

concepts.name: Escalation and handover
concepts.summary: Decide when to escalate and hand over with full context so the customer does not repeat their story.

concepts.name: Prioritising and managing workload
concepts.summary: Order competing contacts and follow-ups by urgency, impact and promised deadlines.

concepts.name: Policy and the customer's interest
concepts.summary: Weigh policy rules against the customer's situation to explain limits clearly or request justified exceptions.

concepts.name: Saying no constructively
concepts.summary: Decline a request while explaining why and offering workable alternatives.

misconceptions.text: The customer's stated complaint is always the real problem.
The way to calm an angry customer is to quickly explain why they are wrong or cite policy.
Escalating a case means you have failed and should be avoided.

concepts.name: Customer effort and journey analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse a customer's end-to-end journey to find points of friction, repeat contacts and effort that can be removed.

concepts.name: Service metrics interpretation
concepts.summary: Evaluate what measures such as satisfaction, first-contact resolution and handling time do and do not tell you, and their trade-offs.

concepts.name: Complaint pattern analysis
concepts.summary: Categorise contacts and feedback to find recurring causes and prioritise those worth fixing at source.

concepts.name: Tailoring approach to customer type
concepts.summary: Judge and adapt communication style and solution to vulnerable, expert, repeat or high-value customers.

concepts.name: Proactive service
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to contact customers before they complain, such as about delays, to prevent contacts and build trust.

concepts.name: Coaching colleagues on service quality
concepts.summary: Review interactions against quality criteria and give specific, constructive feedback that improves a colleague's practice.

concepts.name: Legal and fairness obligations
concepts.summary: Analyse how consumer rights, privacy and fair-treatment duties constrain what you can say, share and offer.

misconceptions.text: A high satisfaction score means service is good, so no further analysis is needed.
Shorter handling time always indicates better service.
Handling each complaint well makes analysing patterns unnecessary.

concepts.name: Cost-to-serve versus value trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate how investment in service levels, automation and self-service balances cost against loyalty and retention.

concepts.name: Building a service culture
concepts.summary: Create hiring, training, empowerment and recognition practices that make good service the norm rather than individual heroics.

concepts.name: Human and automated service blend
concepts.summary: Design how self-service, bots and human agents work together, with consistent context and smooth handoffs across channels.

concepts.name: Crisis and mass-failure response
concepts.summary: Judge and lead communication and remediation when a widespread failure hits many customers at once.

concepts.name: Closing the feedback loop
concepts.summary: Create a system that turns customer insight into prioritised product and process changes and tells customers what changed.

concepts.name: Evaluating service quality frameworks
concepts.summary: Critique and refine quality scorecards and measures so they reward real outcomes and avoid gaming.

concepts.name: Designing a service strategy
concepts.summary: Create a service model that sets standards, channels, staffing and promises aligned with the organisation's strategy and customers' needs.

misconceptions.text: Automating as much service as possible always lowers cost and keeps customers satisfied.
Service quality is the responsibility of the service team alone.
A strict scorecard guarantees good service because staff will follow it.
